text:
sara (sales): hey sec team — just got a weird Google Drive share that claims to be from finance (finance@redwood-payments.com). clicked the link to view an invoice but did NOT enter any creds. it popped an OAuth consent: 'Redwood Tools wants to view your Drive' and i accidentally hit Allow. link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123?usp=sharing

emily (sec): thanks sara. do not use that device for other sensitive stuff. can you paste the original email headers / raw message or screenshot of the consent screen? did it show 'This app isn't verified' or any odd domain on the consent?

sara (sales): attaching screenshot in thread (i'll DM if needed). consent window text looked generic: 'Redwood Tools would like to: View and manage the files in your Google Drive' — there was a tiny publisher 'redwood-tools.app' that looked... off. no "unverified" banner but it was small. raw header snippet i copied: ```Received: from mail-oi1-f65.google.com (mail-oi1-f65.google.com. [209.85.******])
From: "Finance Team" <finance@redwood-payments.com>
Reply-To: finance@redwood-payments.com
Subject: Invoice Approval Needed
To: sara@redwood.com
Message-ID: <CA+abc123@mail.gmail.com>
```

jack (it-admin): thanks. i'm pulling the Admin console now. can you confirm your account email? sara@redwood.com? i'll look for OAuth grants and revoke the client if it's malicious.

sara (sales): yep sara@redwood.com

sec-bot: Automated detection: new OAuth consent grant observed for user=sara@redwood.com client_id=123abc client_name="Redwood Tools" redirect_uri=https://redwood-tools.app/oauth scopes=[https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file, openid, email] risk_score=0.87. Observed at 1777777782.

emily (sec): good catch bot. jack — if you can, revoke the token for that client_id and block that client at org-level. also check Drive audit logs for any files accessed/created/shared by that client_id in the last hour.

jack (it-admin): done: revoked user grant and applied OAuth client block for client_id=123abc (admin console). also forced immediate reauth for sara. commands for record: ```gadmin oauth revoke --client 123abc --user sara@redwood.com``` (console action taken too).

jack (it-admin): checked Drive audit events: earliest access from that client_id = 1777777784, files enumerated but no file downloads or external shares detected. only metadata reads on folder abc123 (the malicious folder). sara did not upload any tokens to 3rd parties.

emily (sec): good. can SRE/infra check sign-in logs for possible token exchange to other apps or IPs? also confirm no admin API calls using our service accounts in last hour. dave?

dave (eng-sre): checking cloud audit logs and GSuite admin logs now. quick summary: client_id 123abc only issued to sara's account, no further cross-account use found. no unusual IAM key activity. KMS logs: no customer-managed key usage tied to this event. looks contained.

emily (sec): thanks. action items: 1) notify sara and confirm no creds entered (confirmed), 2) revoke & block (done), 3) scan sara's Drive for any newly shared links (jack done), 4) search org logs for same client_id or domain (dave done) — all clear. we'll follow up with targeted awareness.

jack (it-admin): filed internal ticket IT-548: 'Block malicious OAuth apps & review OAuth allowlist'. recommending we enforce app allowlisting for org and roll out to high-risk groups first.

emily (sec): post-incident follow-ups: - send a short org-aware note to the team that a suspicious consent prompt circulated; avoid naming the phishing domain publicly, - drafting an FAQ: how to spot OAuth consent phish and how to revoke grants (link to admin steps), - add detection rule: alert on OAuth grants where client_name includes suspicious keywords or client_id not in allowlist + risk_score > 0.7.

sec-bot: Suggestion: create a detection to correlate new OAuth grants with incoming email header SPF/DKIM failures. would have flagged this email earlier.

emily (sec): yep, add correlation to the hunt playbook. also let's include this sample (headers + client_id 123abc) in the phish training simulation.

sara (sales): thanks all. appreciate the fast response. i'll watch my account and let you know if anything odd pops up. :relieved:

emily (sec): thanks sara — closing thread for now. we'll ping the channel when the awareness note and detection are live. :white_check_mark:
